title: Two Discrete Ln12 Shelf-Shaped Clusters: Magnetic Studies Reveal a Significant Cryogenic Magnetocaloric Effect and Slow Magnetic Relaxation

synthesis.procedure: A solution of o-vanillin (0.0304 g, 0.2 mmol), 2-aminoethanol (0.0122 g, 0.2 mmol), and Et3N (0.0404 g, 0.4 mmol) in MeOH (10 mL) was gradually added to a stirred solution of GdCl3·6H2O (0.0744 g, 0.20 mmol) and NaPiv (0.0330 g, 0.3 mmol) in MeCN (10 mL). The resulting yellow solution was stirred under ambient conditions for 4 h and then filtered. The filtrate was left undisturbed to concentrate slowly by solvent evaporation. X-ray quality crystals of Gd12 slowly grew over 1 week and were collected by filtration, washed with cold MeOH, and dried under air. The cluster was obtained by a one-pot reaction at pH ≈ 8; carbonate ligands were attributed to atmospheric CO2 fixation.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility shows χmT = 94.46 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature, remaining nearly constant to 50 K then falling to 65.58 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K; Curie–Weiss fit gives C = 94.33 cm3 K mol−1 and θ = −0.87 K, indicating weak antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd coupling. Magnetization at 2 K and 7 T is 76.45 Nβ (below 84 Nβ for ferromagnetic alignment). Isofield reduced-magnetization curves nearly superimpose, consistent with weak anisotropy. Magnetic entropy change reaches −ΔSm = 30.99 J kg−1 K−1 at 4 K and 7 T, below the theoretical 40.81 J kg−1 K−1 (24.95R) maximum, identifying Gd12 as a cryogenic magnetocaloric candidate.

synthesis.procedure: Obtained by the same one-pot procedure as Gd12, replacing GdCl3·6H2O with DyCl3·6H2O. A MeOH solution of o-vanillin, 2-aminoethanol, and Et3N was added to a MeCN solution of the Dy salt and NaPiv, stirred under ambient conditions for 4 h, filtered, and crystallized by slow evaporation over 1 week. Yellow crystals were collected by filtration, washed with cold MeOH, and dried in air.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χmT = 170.36 cm3 K mol−1 matches 12 uncoupled DyIII ions, remaining constant to 58 K then decreasing to 160.11 cm3 K mol−1 at 5 K and 131.22 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with antiferromagnetic interactions and/or Stark-level depopulation. Magnetization at 2 K and 7 T is 74.79 Nβ, far below 120 Nβ, and M vs H/T curves do not superimpose, indicating anisotropy. Zero-dc-field ac susceptibility (2.0 Oe, 100–1000 Hz) shows frequency-dependent χ′ and χ″ without χ″ maxima, attributed to fast QTM; a 5 kOe dc field did not produce clear frequency-dependent χ″ peaks. Approximate Debye analysis gave Ueff = 3.5 K and τ0 = 0.12 × 10−6 s; Cole–Cole fits support a single relaxation process with α < 0.21. Weak SMM/slow-relaxation behavior is thus observed.
